Lines 1-8: I climb the ladder, kneel, and rake the hay, / and check the apples in the hazy dawn, / in paper, each one wrapped and laid away. / The roof beams hold the snow which veils the lawn. / Each week I come and see each cheek less red, / and hold them, pressing where the peel is thin. / One mark, one more. The blemishes have spread; / decay is moving deep below the skin.
